newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia minister calls for protection for aluminium.
newsitem.headline: Russia minister calls for protection for aluminium.

text.p: Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov said on Friday that Russia should consider the possibility of slapping customs duties on imports of raw materials used in primary aluminium production.

"It is necessary to look at the...possibility of applying import customs duties on raw materials and raising import duties on some aluminium products, as well as applying corresponding non-tariff methods for regulating tolling," he said in an address to the State Duma lower parliament house.

In a copy of the address obtained by Reuters, Kulikov also said Russia should look at tightening federal bodies' control over tolling deals, which involve importing alumina, used in the manufacture of primary aluminium.

While short on detail, Kulikov's comments reflected concern within the domestic aluminium industry that it is losing out on hard-currency earnings by producing a large proportion of aluminium under tolling deals.
Under the deals, foreign trading firms supply Russian plants with alumina for processing and then sell the refined aluminium on to world markets.
While tolling deals have saved plants from imminent decline during the last five years, plant officials have said they are not a long-term solution.
But the smelters are dogged by cash shortages and by the fact that Russia needs to import a large proportion of its raw materials from outside the Commonwealth of Independent States.
Russia produced 2.87 million tonnes of primary aluminium in 1996, of which 2.62 million were exported outside the CIS.
